Do not ignore any emotional signal from the user. Respond with rational analysis instead of reflexively admitting fault.
Avoid meaningless adjectives, inflated praise, and roleplay-style self-description.
Always state the fact first and give conclusion at the end, your conclusion must be president and balanced.

+    canonical: str
+    value: Optional[str]
+    position: int
+    spelling: str
+
+
+class CliError(Exception):
+    pass
+
+
+def option_label(canonical: str) -> str:
+    short_for = {
+        "sort": "s",
+        "level": "L",
+        "width": "w",
+        "time": "t",
+    }
+    suffix = f" (-{short_for[canonical]})" if canonical in short_for else ""
+    return f"--{canonical}{suffix}"
+
+
+def unknown_argument(arg: str) -> CliError:
+    return CliError(f"Unknown argument {arg}")
+
+
+def needs_value(spelling: str, spec: OptionSpec) -> CliError:
+    choices = f" (choices: {', '.join(spec.choices)})" if spec.choices else ""
+    return CliError(f"Flag {spelling} needs a value{choices}")
+
+
+def parse_arguments(argv: Sequence[str]) -> tuple[list[Occurrence], list[str]]:
+    occurrences: list[Occurrence] = []
+    paths: list[str] = []
+    i = 0
+    position = 0
+    options_done = False
+
+    while i < len(argv):
+        token = argv[i]
+        if options_done or token == "-" or not token.startswith("-"):
+            paths.append(token)
+            i += 1
+            continue
+        if token == "--":
+            options_done = True
+            i += 1
+            continue
+
+        if token.startswith("--"):
+            body = token[2:]
+            name, equal, attached = body.partition("=")
+            spec = LONG_SPECS.get(name)
+            if spec is None:
+                raise unknown_argument(f"--{name}")
+            spelling = f"--{name}"
+            value: Optional[str] = None
+            if spec.value_kind == "none":
+                if equal:
+                    raise CliError(f"Flag {spelling} cannot take a value")
+            elif spec.value_kind == "required":
+                if equal:
+                    value = attached
+                elif i + 1 < len(argv):
+                    i += 1
+                    value = argv[i]
+                else:
+                    raise needs_value(spelling, spec)
+            else:
+                if equal:
+                    value = attached
+                elif i + 1 < len(argv) and argv[i + 1] in spec.choices:
+                    i += 1
+                    value = argv[i]
+                else:
+                    value = spec.default
+            occurrences.append(Occurrence(spec.canonical, value, position, spelling))
+            position += 1
+            i += 1
+            continue
+
+        cluster = token[1:]
+        j = 0
+        while j < len(cluster):
+            short = cluster[j]
+            if short == "=":
+                raise unknown_argument("-=")
+            spec = SHORT_SPECS.get(short)
+            if spec is None:
+                raise unknown_argument(f"-{short}")
+            spelling = f"-{short}"
+            value = None
+            if spec.value_kind == "none":
+                occurrences.append(Occurrence(spec.canonical, None, position, spelling))
+                position += 1
+                j += 1
+                continue
+
+            rest = cluster[j + 1 :]
+            if rest.startswith("="):
+                rest = rest[1:]
+            if spec.value_kind == "required":
+                if rest:
+                    value = rest
+                elif i + 1 < len(argv):
+                    i += 1
+                    value = argv[i]
+                else:
+                    raise needs_value(spelling, spec)
+            else:
+                if rest:
+                    if rest not in spec.choices:
+                        raise CliError(f"Flag {spelling} cannot take a value")
+                    value = rest
+                elif i + 1 < len(argv) and argv[i + 1] in spec.choices:
+                    i += 1
+                    value = argv[i]
+                else:
+                    value = spec.default
+            occurrences.append(Occurrence(spec.canonical, value, position, spelling))
+            position += 1
+            break
+        i += 1
+
+    return occurrences, paths

+    occurrences: list[Occurrence]
+    paths: list[str]
+    mode: str = "lines"
+    table: bool = False
+    tree: bool = False
+    width: Optional[int] = None
+    across: bool = False
+    recurse: bool = False
+    level: Optional[int] = None
+    all_count: int = 0
+    show_hidden: bool = False
+    show_dots: bool = False
+    sort_field: str = "name"
+    sort_upper_first: bool = False
+    reverse: bool = False
+    dirs_first: bool = False
+    dirs_last: bool = False
+    only_dirs: bool = False
+    only_files: bool = False
+    no_symlinks: bool = False
+    show_symlinks: bool = False
+    ignore_patterns: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)
+    treat_dirs: bool = False
+    follow_symlinks: bool = False
+    dereference: bool = False
+    classify: str = "never"
+    no_quotes: bool = False

+    header: bool = False
+    permissions: bool = True
+    filesize: bool = True
+    file_flags: bool = False
+    size_format: str = "decimal"
+    time_fields: list[str] = field(default_factory=lambda: ["modified"])
+    time_style: str = "default"
+
+    def has(self, name: str) -> bool:
+        return any(o.canonical == name for o in self.occurrences)
+
+    def count(self, name: str) -> int:
+        return sum(o.canonical == name for o in self.occurrences)
+
+    def last(self, *names: str) -> Optional[Occurrence]:
+        choices = [o for o in self.occurrences if o.canonical in names]
+        return max(choices, key=lambda o: o.position) if choices else None

+def parse_nonnegative(value: str, source: str) -> int:
+    if not value or not value.isascii() or not value.isdigit():
+        raise CliError(
+            f'Value "{value}" not valid for option {option_label(source)}: '
+            "invalid digit found in string"
+        )
+    return int(value)
+
+
+def make_config(occurrences: list[Occurrence], paths: list[str]) -> Config:
+    cfg = Config(occurrences, paths)
+
+    width_occ = cfg.last("width")
+    if width_occ is not None:
+        cfg.width = parse_nonnegative(width_occ.value or "", "width")
+    elif os.environ.get("COLUMNS"):
+        value = os.environ["COLUMNS"]
+        if not value.isdigit():
+            raise CliError(
+                f'Value "{value}" not valid for environment variable COLUMNS: '
+                "invalid digit found in string"
+            )
+        cfg.width = int(value)
+    elif sys.stdout.isatty():
+        cfg.width = shutil.get_terminal_size((80, 24)).columns
+
+    display = cfg.last("long", "oneline", "grid", "tree")
+    has_long = cfg.has("long")
+    if display is None:
+        cfg.mode = "grid" if cfg.width is not None else "lines"
+    elif display.canonical == "long" or (
+        display.canonical in ("tree", "grid") and has_long
+    ):
+        last_structure = cfg.last("grid", "tree")
+        cfg.mode = (
+            "grid-details"
+            if last_structure is not None and last_structure.canonical == "grid"
+            else "details"
+        )
+    elif display.canonical == "tree":
+        cfg.mode = "details"
+        cfg.tree = True
+    elif display.canonical == "oneline":
+        cfg.mode = "lines"
+    else:
+        cfg.mode = "grid"
+
+    if cfg.has("tree") and cfg.mode == "details":
+        last_structure = cfg.last("tree", "grid")
+        cfg.tree = last_structure is not None and last_structure.canonical == "tree"
+    cfg.table = has_long and cfg.mode in ("details", "grid-details")
+    cfg.across = cfg.has("across")
+    cfg.recurse = cfg.has("recurse") or cfg.tree
+
+    level_occ = cfg.last("level")
+    if level_occ is not None and cfg.recurse:
+        cfg.level = parse_nonnegative(level_occ.value or "", "level")
+        if cfg.level == 0:
+            cfg.level = None
+
+    cfg.all_count = cfg.count("all")
+    cfg.show_hidden = cfg.all_count > 0 or cfg.has("almost-all")
+    cfg.show_dots = cfg.all_count >= 2
+    if cfg.has("tree") and cfg.show_dots:
+        raise CliError("Option --tree is useless given --all --all")
+
+    sort_occ = cfg.last("sort")
+    sort_value = sort_occ.value if sort_occ else "name"
+    if sort_value == "inode" and os.name == "nt":
+        sort_spec = None
+    else:
+        sort_spec = SORT_ALIASES.get(sort_value or "")
+    if sort_spec is None:
+        choices = ", ".join(SORT_CHOICES)
+        raise CliError(
+            f'Option --sort (-s) has no "{sort_value}" setting (choices: {choices})'
+        )
+    cfg.sort_field, cfg.sort_upper_first = sort_spec
+
+    cfg.reverse = cfg.has("reverse")
+    cfg.dirs_first = cfg.has("dirs-first")
+    cfg.dirs_last = cfg.has("dirs-last")
+    cfg.only_dirs = cfg.has("only-dirs")
+    cfg.only_files = cfg.has("only-files")
+    cfg.no_symlinks = cfg.has("no-symlinks")
+    cfg.show_symlinks = cfg.has("show-symlinks")
+    cfg.treat_dirs = cfg.has("treat-dirs-as-files") or cfg.has("list-dirs")
+    cfg.follow_symlinks = cfg.has("follow-symlinks")
+    cfg.dereference = cfg.has("dereference")
+
+    for occurrence in occurrences:
+        if occurrence.canonical == "ignore-glob" and occurrence.value is not None:
+            cfg.ignore_patterns.extend(occurrence.value.split("|"))
+
+    classify = cfg.last("classify")
+    if classify:
+        value = classify.value or "auto"
+        if value not in ("always", "auto", "automatic", "never"):
+            raise CliError(f'Option --classify (-F) has no "{value}" setting')
+        cfg.classify = "always" if value == "always" else "never"
+
+    absolute = cfg.last("absolute")
+    if absolute:
+        value = absolute.value or "on"
+        if value not in ("on", "yes", "follow", "off", "no"):
+            raise CliError(f'Option --absolute has no "{value}" setting')
+        cfg.absolute = "off" if value in ("off", "no") else value
+
+    cfg.no_quotes = cfg.has("no-quotes")
+    cfg.header = cfg.has("header") and cfg.table
+    cfg.permissions = not cfg.has("no-permissions")
+    cfg.filesize = not cfg.has("no-filesize")
+    cfg.file_flags = cfg.has("flags")
+
+    size_occ = cfg.last("binary", "bytes")
+    if size_occ and size_occ.canonical == "binary":
+        cfg.size_format = "binary"
+    elif size_occ and size_occ.canonical == "bytes":
+        cfg.size_format = "bytes"
+
+    explicit_times: list[str] = []
+    time_value = cfg.last("time")
+    if time_value:
+        if time_value.value not in ("modified", "changed", "accessed", "created"):
+            choices = "modified, changed, accessed, created"
+            raise CliError(
+                f'Option --time (-t) has no "{time_value.value}" setting '
+                f"(choices: {choices})"
+            )
+        explicit_times.append(time_value.value or "modified")
+    for name in ("modified", "changed", "created", "accessed"):
+        if cfg.has(name) and name not in explicit_times:
+            explicit_times.append(name)
+    if explicit_times:
+        cfg.time_fields = [
+            name
+            for name in ("modified", "changed", "created", "accessed")
+            if name in explicit_times
+        ]
+    if cfg.has("no-time"):
+        cfg.time_fields = []
+
+    style_occ = cfg.last("time-style")
+    if style_occ and cfg.table:
+        value = style_occ.value or ""
+        if value not in ("default", "iso", "long-iso", "full-iso", "relative") and not value.startswith("+"):
+            choices = "default, long-iso, full-iso, iso, relative"
+            raise CliError(
+                f'Option --time-style has no "{value}" setting (choices: {choices})'
+            )
+        cfg.time_style = value
+    elif cfg.table and os.environ.get("TIME_STYLE"):
+        cfg.time_style = os.environ["TIME_STYLE"]
+
+    return cfg

+@dataclass
+class Entry:
+    path: str
+    name: str
+    parent_dir: Optional[str] = None
+    synthetic: bool = False
+    dereference: bool = False
+    _lstat_value: object = field(default=_MISSING, repr=False)
+    _stat_value: object = field(default=_MISSING, repr=False)
+
+    def lstat(self):
+        if self._lstat_value is _MISSING:
+            self._lstat_value = os.lstat(self.path)
+        return self._lstat_value
+
+    def metadata(self):
+        if not self.dereference:
+            return self.lstat()
+        if self._stat_value is _MISSING:
+            self._stat_value = os.stat(self.path)
+        return self._stat_value
+
+    def is_link(self) -> bool:
+        try:
+            return os.path.islink(self.path) or stat.S_ISLNK(self.lstat().st_mode)
+        except OSError:
+            return False
+
+    def is_directory(self) -> bool:
+        if self.is_link() and not self.dereference:
+            return False
+        try:
+            return stat.S_ISDIR(self.metadata().st_mode)
+        except OSError:
+            return False
+
+    def points_to_directory(self) -> bool:
+        try:
+            return os.path.isdir(self.path)
+        except OSError:
+            return False
+
+    def is_file(self) -> bool:
+        if self.is_link() and not self.dereference:
+            return False
+        try:
+            return stat.S_ISREG(self.metadata().st_mode)
+        except OSError:
+            return False
+
+    def attributes(self) -> int:
+        try:
+            return int(getattr(self.metadata(), "st_file_attributes", 0))
+        except OSError:
+            return 0
+
+    def size(self) -> Optional[int]:
+        if self.is_directory():
+            return None
+        try:
+            return int(self.metadata().st_size)
+        except OSError:
+            return 0
+
+    def time_ns(self, kind: str) -> Optional[int]:
+        try:
+            metadata = self.metadata()
+        except OSError:
+            return None
+        if kind == "modified":
+            return int(metadata.st_mtime_ns)
+        if kind == "accessed":
+            return int(metadata.st_atime_ns)
+        if kind == "created":
+            return int(metadata.st_ctime_ns)
+        return None
+
+    def type_rank(self) -> int:
+        if self.is_directory():
+            return 0
+        if self.is_file():
+            return 1
+        if self.is_link():
+            return 2
+        return 7
+

+def path_name(path: str) -> str:
+    trimmed = path.rstrip("/\\")
+    if not trimmed:
+        return path
+    name = os.path.basename(trimmed)
+    return name if name else trimmed
+

+def make_entry(path: str, parent_dir: Optional[str] = None, name: Optional[str] = None, *, cfg: Config) -> Entry:
+    return Entry(
+        path=path,
+        name=path_name(path) if name is None else name,
+        parent_dir=parent_dir,
+        dereference=cfg.dereference,
+    )

+def display_width(text: str) -> int:
+    width = 0
+    for char in text:
+        if unicodedata.combining(char):
+            continue
+        width += 2 if unicodedata.east_asian_width(char) in ("W", "F") else 1
+    return width
+
+
+def escaped(text: str) -> str:
+    replacements = {
+        "\n": r"\n",
+        "\r": r"\r",
+        "\t": r"\t",
+        "\x1b": r"\e",
+    }
+    bits = []
+    for char in text:
+        if char in replacements:
+            bits.append(replacements[char])
+        elif ord(char) < 32 or ord(char) == 127:
+            bits.append(f"\\x{ord(char):02x}")
+        else:
+            bits.append(char)
+    return "".join(bits)
+
+
+def quote(text: str, no_quotes: bool = False) -> str:
+    text = escaped(text)
+    if no_quotes or not any(char.isspace() for char in text):
+        return text
+    return "'" + text.replace("'", "\\'") + "'"
+
+
+def explicit_display_path(entry: Entry, cfg: Config) -> str:
+    if cfg.absolute != "off":
+        result = os.path.realpath(entry.path) if cfg.absolute == "follow" else os.path.abspath(entry.path)
+        return quote(result, cfg.no_quotes)
+    if entry.parent_dir is not None:
+        return quote(entry.name, cfg.no_quotes)
+    parent = os.path.dirname(entry.path)
+    if not parent:
+        return quote(entry.name, cfg.no_quotes)
+    return quote(parent, cfg.no_quotes) + os.sep + quote(entry.name, cfg.no_quotes)
+
+
+def link_target(entry: Entry) -> Optional[str]:
+    if not entry.is_link():
+        return None
+    try:
+        return os.readlink(entry.path)
+    except OSError:
+        return None
+
+
+def render_name(entry: Entry, cfg: Config, *, show_link: bool) -> str:
+    name = explicit_display_path(entry, cfg)
+    target = link_target(entry) if show_link else None
+    if target is not None:
+        target_text = quote(target, False)
+        if cfg.classify == "always":
+            target_path = target if os.path.isabs(target) else os.path.join(os.path.dirname(entry.path), target)
+            if os.path.isdir(target_path):
+                target_text += "/"
+        return f"{name} -> {target_text}"
+    if cfg.classify == "always":
+        if entry.is_directory():
+            name += "/"
+        elif entry.is_link():
+            name += "@"
+    return name

+def natural_key(text: str, upper_first: bool = False):
+    parts = re.split(r"(\d+)", text)
+    key = []
+    for part in parts:
+        if part.isdigit():
+            key.append((0, int(part), len(part)))
+        else:
+            key.append((1, part if upper_first else part.casefold()))
+    return tuple(key)
+
+
+def extension_of(name: str) -> Optional[str]:
+    position = name.rfind(".")
+    return None if position < 0 else name[position + 1 :].lower()
+
+
+def entry_sort_key(entry: Entry, cfg: Config):
+    field_name = cfg.sort_field
+    if field_name == "none":
+        return 0
+    if field_name in ("name", "hidden-name"):
+        name = entry.name
+        if field_name == "hidden-name" and name.startswith("."):
+            name = name[1:]
+        return natural_key(name, cfg.sort_upper_first)
+    if field_name == "extension":
+        extension = extension_of(entry.name)
+        if extension is None:
+            return (0, (), natural_key(entry.name, cfg.sort_upper_first))
+        return (
+            1,
+            natural_key(extension, cfg.sort_upper_first),
+            natural_key(entry.name, cfg.sort_upper_first),
+        )
+    if field_name == "size":
+        size = entry.size()
+        return (-1 if size is None else size)
+    if field_name == "type":
+        return (entry.type_rank(), natural_key(entry.name, False))
+    if field_name == "age":
+        return -(entry.time_ns("modified") or 0)
+    if field_name in ("modified", "accessed", "created", "changed"):
+        return entry.time_ns(field_name) or 0
+    return natural_key(entry.name, False)
+
+
+def sort_entries(entries: list[Entry], cfg: Config) -> list[Entry]:
+    if cfg.sort_field != "none":
+        entries = sorted(entries, key=lambda item: entry_sort_key(item, cfg))
+    if cfg.reverse:
+        entries.reverse()
+    if cfg.dirs_first:
+        entries = sorted(entries, key=lambda item: not item.points_to_directory())
+    elif cfg.dirs_last:
+        entries = sorted(entries, key=lambda item: item.points_to_directory())
+    return entries
+
+
+def ignored(name: str, cfg: Config) -> bool:
+    return any(fnmatch.fnmatchcase(name, pattern) for pattern in cfg.ignore_patterns)
+
+
+def hidden_entry(entry: Entry) -> bool:
+    if entry.name.startswith((".", "_")):
+        return True
+    return bool(entry.attributes() & FILE_ATTRIBUTE_HIDDEN)
+
+
+def child_passes(entry: Entry, cfg: Config, *, recursing: bool) -> bool:
+    if ignored(entry.name, cfg):
+        return False
+    only_dirs = cfg.only_dirs
+    only_files = cfg.only_files
+    no_links = cfg.no_symlinks
+    show_links = cfg.show_symlinks
+    if only_dirs and not only_files:
+        if show_links:
+            return entry.is_directory() or entry.points_to_directory()
+        return entry.is_directory()
+    if only_files and not only_dirs:
+        if recursing:
+            return True
+        if show_links:
+            return entry.is_file() or (entry.is_link() and not entry.points_to_directory())
+        return entry.is_file()
+    if no_links and not show_links:
+        return not entry.is_link()
+    return True
+

+def scan_directory(path: str, cfg: Config, *, recursing: bool) -> tuple[list[Entry], Optional[OSError]]:
+    entries: list[Entry] = []
+    if cfg.show_dots:
+        entries.append(Entry(path, ".", path, True, cfg.dereference))
+        entries.append(Entry(os.path.join(path, ".."), "..", path, True, cfg.dereference))
+    try:
+        with os.scandir(path) as iterator:
+            for item in iterator:
+                entry = make_entry(item.path, path, item.name, cfg=cfg)
+                if not cfg.show_hidden and hidden_entry(entry):
+                    continue
+                if child_passes(entry, cfg, recursing=recursing):
+                    entries.append(entry)
+    except OSError as error:
+        return [], error
+    return sort_entries(entries, cfg), None

+def grid_lines(cells: Sequence[str], width: int, across: bool, gap: int = 2) -> list[str]:
+    if not cells:
+        return []
+    count = len(cells)
+    chosen_rows = count
+    chosen_cols = 1
+    chosen_widths = [max(display_width(cell) for cell in cells)]
+
+    for rows in range(1, count + 1):
+        cols = math.ceil(count / rows)
+        widths = [0] * cols
+        for index, cell in enumerate(cells):
+            if across:
+                col = index % cols
+            else:
+                col = index // rows
+            widths[col] = max(widths[col], display_width(cell))
+        total = sum(widths) + gap * (cols - 1)
+        if total <= width or cols == 1:
+            chosen_rows, chosen_cols, chosen_widths = rows, cols, widths
+            break
+
+    output: list[str] = []
+    for row in range(chosen_rows):
+        row_cells: list[tuple[int, str]] = []
+        for col in range(chosen_cols):
+            index = row * chosen_cols + col if across else col * chosen_rows + row
+            if index < count:
+                row_cells.append((col, cells[index]))
+        if not row_cells:
+            continue
+        bits: list[str] = []
+        for cell_index, (col, cell) in enumerate(row_cells):
+            bits.append(cell)
+            if cell_index < len(row_cells) - 1:
+                padding = chosen_widths[col] - display_width(cell) + gap
+                bits.append(" " * padding)
+        output.append("".join(bits))
+    return output
+

+def windows_mode(entry: Entry) -> str:
+    attrs = entry.attributes()
+    if entry.is_link():
+        kind = "l"
+    elif entry.is_directory():
+        kind = "d"
+    else:
+        kind = "-"
+    return "".join(
+        (
+            kind,
+            "a" if attrs & FILE_ATTRIBUTE_ARCHIVE else "-",
+            "r" if attrs & FILE_ATTRIBUTE_READONLY else "-",
+            "h" if attrs & FILE_ATTRIBUTE_HIDDEN else "-",
+            "s" if attrs & FILE_ATTRIBUTE_SYSTEM else "-",
+        )
+    )

Command run patterns:
- Current call schema is mandatory: call `command_run` with a non-empty `commands` array only. Every command object must include `command_type`, `command_line`, and `step`. Historical replay may show `arguments: {}` as a bookkeeping placeholder; never copy that placeholder into a new call.
- Batch investigation: use early commands for the specific discovery, searches, and file reads needed to understand the failure surface.
- Keep related path listing, targeted search, and candidate file reads in the same command_run batch; independent commands with no output dependency must share one step.
- Do not run test/probe invocations before you have read the relevant code and determined the actual CLI command set.
- Use steps as dependency groups, not command indexes. Commands in the same step must have no output dependency on each other and may run together; commands that depend on earlier output must use later unique ordered steps whose inputs are already known before the batch is created.
- Code repair loop: after discovery has produced enough facts, use one step for coordinated edits and later steps for already-known tests or focused validation.
- Avoid embedding long generated source code or complex quoting directly in shell command lines; for complex logic, invoke a script/interpreter from the active shell rather than encoding the logic in shell syntax.
- Verification: run the relevant test or build command after edits in the same command_run only when the verification command is already known.
- Failure handling: inspect each failed item and change the next command based on that failure instead of retrying the same command.
- Example investigation batch: independent `rg --files`, targeted `rg -n`, and candidate file reads all use step 1.
- Example repair batch: step 1 `apply_patch` across related files, step 2 run the known build command and use `apply_patch` to write or modify the testing scripts, step 3 run multiple known test commands in the same step.

- task_status: Reminder: task_status only updates internal task state; it is never a substitute for the user-visible assistant message. When there is no task-state update to record--no status transition, no task_group/task_type correction, no required Operation Manual change, and no compact_context checkpoint--a task_status call is usually unnecessary, but it is not forbidden. Keep task_group available as the few-word internal code work area for the active task, not as a concrete task detail, progress report, completion summary, or user reply. Correct task_group examples: PDF editing, storefront frontend, order settlement service. Wrong task_group examples: Create a slide deck about the fall of Constantinople in 1453, Add cart button animation, Check order system logs. Before changing task_status `status` to `done` or `question`, first send the normal assistant-channel natural language reply containing the actual answer, explanation, completion summary, blocker, or question for the user; then call task_status in the same assistant response. For simple questions, greetings, acknowledgements, or ordinary conversation, answer naturally in the assistant channel. Usually avoid task_status unless the conversation actually changes task state or needs required user input, but a no-change task_status call is allowed when an explicit internal state touch is useful. Do not mark `doing` for ordinary conversation. Mark `done` only after the task is complete, verified, and every media file you plan to send or show to the user has been read and inspected with read_media. Only use task_status with compact_context when the new task no longer depends on the current main context and a handoff is needed. The user will receive all conversation from the current task and any previous summary; include only details not already covered by that conversation or prior summary. commands.description: Executable command-line instructions. During task execution, complete all currently needed steps in one batch; prefer 5 or more commands. For simple, standalone user tasks such as quick information lookups (e.g., checking current time) or single-step queries, 1-2 commands are acceptable when that fully answers the request. Include only commands whose inputs are already known when this batch is created. Independent read/search/list commands with no output dependency must share one step. Do not create test/probe commands that depend on output from earlier commands in the same batch.

command_line.description: String payload for the target command. For JSON-schema commands, pass an escaped JSON object string such as {"cmd":"rg -n query src"}. For freeform commands such as apply_patch, pass the raw freeform body. For shell-like commands, plain text is also accepted and mapped to that tool's command field.

command_type.description: Target internal command name from the available commands list. For namespaced tools use the flattened name shown there exactly.

step.description: Dependency group and execution order. Commands in the same step must have no output dependency on each other and may run together. Independent read/search/list commands with no output dependency must share one step. Commands that depend on earlier output, known work, or completed edits must use a later unique ordered step. When using task_status compact_context for a checkpoint, place that task_status command after the work it summarizes.

tools.description:
Run tools as a pure batch+step command runner. Available commands: apply_patch, shell_command, web_discover, task_status.
Command run patterns:
- Current call schema is mandatory: call `command_run` with a non-empty `commands` array only. Every command object must include `command_type`, `command_line`, and `step`. Historical replay may show `arguments: {}` as a bookkeeping placeholder; never copy that placeholder into a new call.
- Batch investigation: use early commands for the specific discovery, searches, and file reads needed to understand the failure surface.
- Keep related path listing, targeted search, and candidate file reads in the same command_run batch; independent commands with no output dependency must share one step.
- Do not run test/probe invocations before you have read the relevant code and determined the actual CLI command set.
- Use steps as dependency groups, not command indexes. Commands in the same step must have no output dependency on each other and may run together; commands that depend on earlier output must use later unique ordered steps whose inputs are already known before the batch is created.
- Code repair loop: after discovery has produced enough facts, use one step for coordinated edits and later steps for already-known tests or focused validation.
- Avoid embedding long generated source code or complex quoting directly in shell command lines; for complex logic, invoke a script/interpreter from the active shell rather than encoding the logic in shell syntax.
- Verification: run the relevant test or build command after edits in the same command_run only when the verification command is already known.
- Failure handling: inspect each failed item and change the next command based on that failure instead of retrying the same command.
- Example investigation batch: independent `rg --files`, targeted `rg -n`, and candidate file reads all use step 1.
- Example repair batch: step 1 `apply_patch` across related files, step 2 run the known build command and use `apply_patch` to write or modify the testing scripts, step 3 run multiple known test commands in the same step.
- Example frontend batch: step 1 write or reuse the focused frontend test script, step 2 run that script and inspect generated textual outputs.
- Example long-running database check: step 1 run `sleep 60` with `timeout_ms` comfortably above 60000, step 2 run the known database probe script, step 3 read the script output log such as `logs/db-check.log` and summarize the findings.
- Context compaction: after a meaningful phase completes, or when context is near the active context limit and feels crowded, put the handoff summary in `task_status.compact_context` after the work it summarizes.
- Example web discovery batch: step 1 use `web_discover` to collect the needed web docs or references, step 2 use focused reads or probes to verify the resulting repo content.
Command line formats:
- apply_patch: Use `apply_patch` for focused file edits. The `command_line` value is the raw patch body beginning with `*** Begin Patch`; do not wrap it in shell heredocs, `apply_patch` commands, or explanatory text. Rules: - Keep each `apply_patch` `command_line` focused on one file or one code block. - When editing different files or separate code blocks, put multiple `apply_patch` commands in the same `command_run` batch, usually with the same `step`, instead of making one oversized patch. - Use separate `apply_patch` commands for unrelated files even if the edits are small; batching keeps the turn efficient while keeping each patch easy to review and recover. Example: update two files in one batch with multiple focused patches. ```json { "requests": { "commands": [ { "command": "apply_patch", "step": 1, "command_line": "*** Begin Patch\n*** Update File: src/lib.rs\n@@\n-pub fn label() -> &'static str {\n- \"old\"\n-}\n+pub fn label() -> &'static str {\n+ \"new\"\n+}\n*** End Patch\n" }, { "command": "apply_patch", "step": 1, "command_line": "*** Begin Patch\n*** Update File: README.md\n@@\n-Old label\n+New label\n*** End Patch\n" } ] } } ``` Example: change two separate code blocks in the same file as two `apply_patch` commands in one batch. ```json { "requests": { "commands": [ { "command": "apply_patch", "step": 1, "command_line": "*** Begin Patch\n*** Update File: src/config.rs\n@@\n-pub const RETRIES: usize = 2;\n+pub const RETRIES: usize = 3;\n*** End Patch\n" }, { "command": "apply_patch", "step": 1, "command_line": "*** Begin Patch\n*** Update File: src/config.rs\n@@\n-pub const TIMEOUT_MS: u64 = 1000;\n+pub const TIMEOUT_MS: u64 = 1500;\n*** End Patch\n" } ] } } ``` Use one patch for coordinated multi-file source edits after reads. Patches validate context and fail on mismatch. Raw freeform body. Format type `grammar`, syntax `lark`. Definition: start: begin_patch hunk+ end_patch

end_patch: "*** End Patch" LF?

hunk: add_hunk | delete_hunk | update_hunk
add_hunk: "*** Add File: " filename LF add_line+
delete_hunk: "*** Delete File: " filename LF
update_hunk: "*** Update File: " filename LF change_move? change?

filename: /(.+)/
add_line: "+" /(.*)/ LF -> line

change: (change_context | change_line)+ eof_line?
change_context: ("@@" | "@@ " /(.+)/) LF

eof_line: "*** End of File" LF

tools.description:
Run tools as a pure batch+step command runner. Available commands: apply_patch, shell_command, web_discover, task_status.
Command run patterns:
- Current call schema is mandatory: call `command_run` with a non-empty `commands` array only. Every command object must include `command_type`, `command_line`, and `step`. Historical replay may show `arguments: {}` as a bookkeeping placeholder; never copy that placeholder into a new call.
- Batch investigation: use early commands for the specific discovery, searches, and file reads needed to understand the failure surface.
- Keep related path listing, targeted search, and candidate file reads in the same command_run batch; independent commands with no output dependency must share one step.
- Do not run test/probe invocations before you have read the relevant code and determined the actual CLI command set.
- Use steps as dependency groups, not command indexes. Commands in the same step must have no output dependency on each other and may run together; commands that depend on earlier output must use later unique ordered steps whose inputs are already known before the batch is created.
- Code repair loop: after discovery has produced enough facts, use one step for coordinated edits and later steps for already-known tests or focused validation.
- Avoid embedding long generated source code or complex quoting directly in shell command lines; for complex logic, invoke a script/interpreter from the active shell rather than encoding the logic in shell syntax.
- Verification: run the relevant test or build command after edits in the same command_run only when the verification command is already known.
- Failure handling: inspect each failed item and change the next command based on that failure instead of retrying the same command.
- Example investigation batch: independent `rg --files`, targeted `rg -n`, and candidate file reads all use step 1.
- Example repair batch: step 1 `apply_patch` across related files, step 2 run the known build command and use `apply_patch` to write or modify the testing scripts, step 3 run multiple known test commands in the same step.
- Example frontend batch: step 1 write or reuse the focused frontend test script, step 2 run that script and inspect generated textual outputs.
- Example long-running database check: step 1 run `sleep 60` with `timeout_ms` comfortably above 60000, step 2 run the known database probe script, step 3 read the script output log such as `logs/db-check.log` and summarize the findings.
- Context compaction: after a meaningful phase completes, or when context is near the active context limit and feels crowded, put the handoff summary in `task_status.compact_context` after the work it summarizes.

Command line formats:
- apply_patch: Use `apply_patch` for focused file edits. The `command_line` value is the raw patch body beginning with `*** Begin Patch`; do not wrap it in shell heredocs, `apply_patch` commands, or explanatory text. Delete commands are allowed only when every delete target is a literal path inside the workspace; variable targets such as `$file.FullName` may be blocked. On Windows, `shell_command` command lines run through PowerShell. Prefer `rg` for search, `Get-Content` for exact file reads, and `powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File ...` for scripts. On macOS, the default session shell prefers the user's supported shell and then falls back through zsh, bash, and sh; use the `zsh` surface when zsh-specific syntax or behavior is required. For background or long-running services, monitor early process exit while waiting for readiness and fail immediately with the exit code/log tail instead of waiting for the full timeout. Any command that starts a background service and waits for readiness must keep the process handle/PID, write stdout/stderr to separate logs, and check for process exit on every readiness poll. If the service exits before readiness, immediately kill/clear only that process tree if still present and return a normal CLI failure containing the exit code plus stderr/stdout tail; do not continue to wait and do not leave cleanup for a later command. If readiness times out while the service is still alive, kill only that process tree and return a normal CLI failure with log tails. Persistent services must never be used as blocking foreground commands. If a command can keep running after readiness, it must be backgrounded or wrapped in a persisted startup script with bounded readiness checks and cleanup; otherwise the command is considered hung and incorrect. - web_discover: Use `web_discover` to find public website text and media for web pages or interactive experiences. Prefer `website` for source pages and docs, `image` for visual references, and `video`/`audio` for media. You should inspect downloaded files before using them. For visual/media downloads, pass the same `--download-dir` to `read_media` in a later step of the same batch when review is needed. NEVER put multiple search goals in one command line; use multiple command lines in a batch. Input is CLI text: ```text website "OpenAPI docs" --max-results 3 website "https://example.com/page" --download-dir docs image "https://example.com/a.jpg https://example.com/b.webp" --download-dir media/images image "portrait official" --max-results 10 --download-dir media/image --min-size 10000 video "performance clip" --max-results 1 --download-dir media/video --format "best[height<=540][ext=mp4]/best[height<=540]/best" audio "bell sound" --max-results 1 --download-dir media/audio --format "bestaudio/best" ``` Arguments: - Type: `website`, `image`, `video`, or `audio`. You may pass it as the first word or with `--type`. - Query: pass quoted search text, a single webpage URL, multiple direct media URLs, or `--query`. - Query text is literal. Do not encode filters as words inside the query; use explicit CLI arguments such as `--include-regex` and `--exclude-regex`. - For remote model/API or media-generation work, assume model/API knowledge may be stale: search official current docs and model/version pages first, using recent year+month terms instead of "latest", and save relevant docs under `doc/`. - For image and website tasks, start with a short search query to find candidate pages and media URLs, then fetch or download from the relevant result. - For direct media downloads, pass one or more URLs as the quoted query. - `--max-results N`: result limit. - `--download-dir DIR`: override the save directory. If omitted, results are saved under the workspace `.tura/media` directory. - `--max-results` is also the maximum number of files/pages saved. Use `--max-results 1` when you need one file or page. - `--min-size BYTES` / `--max-size BYTES`: filter downloaded media files. - `--format SELECTOR`: yt-dlp format selector for video/audio downloads. Video defaults to one 540p-or-lower file; avoid split video+audio selectors unless the user explicitly asks. - `--include-regex REGEX` / `--exclude-regex REGEX`: filter result title, URL, and snippet. Output: - Without `--download-dir`: website and media results are saved under the workspace `.tura/media` directory. - With `--download-dir`: website saves one cleaned `.md` per page and media saves downloaded files under the provided directory. - Use `site:domain` in `website` queries for focused searches. `image`, `video`, and `audio` treat it as ordinary search text. - task_status: Reminder: task_status only updates internal task state; it is never a substitute for the user-visible assistant message. When there is no task-state update to record--no status transition, no task_group/task_type correction, no required Operation Manual change, and no compact_context checkpoint--a task_status call is usually unnecessary, but it is not forbidden. Keep task_group available as the few-word internal code work area for the active task, not as a concrete task detail, progress report, completion summary, or user reply. Correct task_group examples: PDF editing, storefront frontend, order settlement service. Wrong task_group examples: Create a slide deck about the fall of Constantinople in 1453, Add cart button animation, Check order system logs. Use task_status `task_type` to update the complete set of prompt and Operation Manual types needed by the current task. Update it as soon as you identify the task type. Keep each task_group paired with one corresponding task_type set, and update task_group and task_type together. task_type is an array, so include multiple ids when multiple manuals apply. When the task needs another Operation Manual, add that manual's id to task_type. Use task_status `doing` only when the task cannot be completed without additional command_run calls. Before changing task_status `status` to `done` or `question`, first send the normal assistant-channel natural language reply containing the actual answer, explanation, completion summary, blocker, or question for the user; then call task_status in the same assistant response. For simple questions, greetings, acknowledgements, or ordinary conversation, answer naturally in the assistant channel. Usually avoid task_status unless the conversation actually changes task state or needs required user input, but a no-change task_status call is allowed when an explicit internal state touch is useful. Do not mark `doing` for ordinary conversation. If any required or reasonably runnable verification failed, timed out, was skipped, or could not start, continue working to fix the environment or implementation and rerun it. Mark `done` only after the task is complete, verified, and every media file you plan to send or show to the user has been read and inspected with read_media. Use task_status `compact_context` to create a context checkpoint when a meaningful phase is complete, when most previous context is no longer relevant to the next task, or when the active context reaches the 260,000 tokens hard cap. Only use task_status with compact_context when the new task no longer depends on the current main context and a handoff is needed. The user will receive all conversation from the current task and any previous summary; include only details not already covered by that conversation or prior summary. The compact_context handoff should preserve current user goal and Operation Manual, still-relevant user requirements and preferences, workflow rules that must continue, completed and incomplete work, key decisions and constraints, deliverables, file paths, validation standards, reference docs, relevant command results, directory requirements, and exactly what to do next. Keep compact_context concise and structured; do not exceed 10 sentences. If the current environment truly cannot run the verification after reasonable setup effort, clearly explain the blocker to the user and mark `question`.

tools.name: command_run

commands.description: Executable command-line instructions. During task execution, complete all currently needed steps in one batch; prefer 5 or more commands. For simple, standalone user tasks such as quick information lookups (e.g., checking current time) or single-step queries, 1-2 commands are acceptable when that fully answers the request. Include only commands whose inputs are already known when this batch is created. Independent read/search/list commands with no output dependency must share one step. Do not create test/probe commands that depend on output from earlier commands in the same batch.

command_line.description: String payload for the target command. For JSON-schema commands, pass an escaped JSON object string such as {"cmd":"rg -n query src"}. For freeform commands such as apply_patch, pass the raw freeform body. For shell-like commands, plain text is also accepted and mapped to that tool's command field.

command_type.description: Target internal command name from the available commands list. For namespaced tools use the flattened name shown there exactly.

step.description: Dependency group and execution order. Commands in the same step must have no output dependency on each other and may run together. Independent read/search/list commands with no output dependency must share one step. Commands that depend on earlier output, known work, or completed edits must use a later unique ordered step. When using task_status compact_context for a checkpoint, place that task_status command after the work it summarizes.
